- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.  
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., 5% or more below), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) after a strong recent peak; add 1–2% to early forecast values if sentiment is bullish.  
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
